Seven cymbals drawn from above and played from one model. Click the bell, the bow or the edge; choke it; pick two and compare. Click a heading to fold or open it.

::: {.ik-do}
**What you'll do**

1. Learn what shapes a cymbal's sound: size, weight, alloy, hammering and lathing, where you hit it.
2. Hear a dark K beside a bright 2002, a ride beside a crash, the hi-hat's four sounds.
3. Translate between cymbals and see what is lost (the hi-hat's pedal has nowhere to go on a ride).
:::

## What shapes a cymbal's sound

- **Partials**: many, long and inharmonic. The model has about seventy, rising faster than a harmonic series, each decaying faster the higher it is (the law and the numbers are the site's: unverified).
- **Size and weight**: bigger is louder with longer sustain; heavier is louder with more cut (Wikipedia, "Cymbal").
- **Alloy**: bell bronze for Zildjian's A and K (Wikipedia, "Cymbal"; the exact recipe is secret, Wikipedia "Zildjian"); 8 % tin B8, Paiste's "2002 bronze" (Wikipedia, "Paiste").
- **Dark and bright**: the K's hand-hammering is called dark, the 2002 bright. Here that is how fast the partials' loudness falls with frequency (and how much it scatters): the spectral centroid is lower for the K. The words are the makers' and drummers'; the numbers are the site's.
- **Where you hit it**: the bow pings, the bell rings, the edge washes and "blooms" as the energy climbs into the high partials.
- **Hi-hats**: closed, half, open, and the foot alone (Wikipedia, "Hi-hat"). **China**: trashy (Wikipedia, "China cymbal"). **Splash**: small and short (Wikipedia, "Splash cymbal").

## Translating

Between two cymbals of the same type the choke carries over and the report gives the brightness difference (centroid of the partials); between types it says what changes; from the hi-hats the pedal is **lost**.

## What is this site's own

- Every number of the model, the colours and the lathing rings of the drawings (no logos). Nobody has compared the sound with real cymbals.

## Works Cited

<!-- works-cited: written by scripts/works-cited.py -->
::: {.works-cited}
"China cymbal." *Wikipedia*, Wikimedia Foundation, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China_cymbal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China_cymbal). Bright, crisp, explosive: "trash cymbal"; mounted bell up or down.

"Crash cymbal." *Wikipedia*, Wikimedia Foundation, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crash_cymbal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crash_cymbal). Accents; short wash.

"Cymbal." *Wikipedia*, Wikimedia Foundation, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cymbal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cymbal). Bigger: louder, longer sustain; heavier: louder, more cut; bell bronze the traditional alloy; B8 = 8 % tin malleable bronze, Paiste's "2002" alloy.

"Paiste." *Wikipedia*, Wikimedia Foundation, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paiste](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paiste). CuSn8 "2002 bronze" (B8) from 1965, the 2002 series; unlathed RUDE 1980; Stewart Copeland and the splash.

"Ride cymbal." *Wikipedia*, Wikimedia Foundation, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ride_cymbal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ride_cymbal). Most common 20" (18-22"); sustained shimmer; bell.

"Splash cymbal." *Wikipedia*, Wikimedia Foundation, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Splash_cymbal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Splash_cymbal). Most common 8" then 10"; Ringo Starr, Stewart Copeland.

"Zildjian." *Wikipedia*, Wikimedia Foundation, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zildjian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zildjian). Founded Constantinople 1623; alloy recipe secret; K Zildjian made in the US from 1975, relaunched with Elvin Jones and Tony Williams.

**For students**

"Hi-hat." *Wikipedia*, Wikimedia Foundation, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hi-hat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hi-hat). Two 13-15" cymbals on a pedal stand; open, closed, pedal (foot) sounds.
:::
<!-- /works-cited -->
